title: Orbit Surgeon Workbench: interactive toolkit for safe ad-hoc runbook tasks
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Summary:
Orbit Surgeon Workbench is a lightweight interactive admin workbench for SREs and first-line support to run curated, parameterized rescue recipes against production systems with safety rails, dry-run rehearsal, and auditable output.

Why this exists:
- Current ad-hoc admin flows are scattered between docs, ad-hoc scripts, and temporary shell sessions. That increases blast radius and slows incident resolution.
- We need a single, discoverable surface where engineers can execute vetted atomic actions, preview effects, and commit with a documented, auditable trail.

Core capabilities:
1) Recipe library: versioned, typed inputs, safe defaults, and idempotency tokens. Recipes are small action graphs (fetch -> validate -> mutate -> verify) but surfaced as a single button/command.
2) Rehearsal mode: dry-run with simulated side-effects and a post-mortem diff report.
3) Scoped credentials: ephemeral elevated tokens with automatic revocation, gated by RBAC and step approval for high-risk recipes.
4) Execution proofs: signed execution logs + snapshot of key metrics (latency, token counts, KV checks) stored in the audit store.
5) Telemetry & rollback signals: per-recipe SLO checks and automatic warm-fallback if critical thresholds are breached.

Non-goals:
- Not a full runbook authoring language. Focus is on curated, small-surface recipes for fast remediation.
- Not replacing large-scale orchestration pipelines (those stay in existing admin-runflow infra).

Success metrics:
- Mean time to first safe remediation (MTFSR) reduced by 35% for Tier 1 incidents during the 6-week pilot.
- 0 critical safety incidents introduced by recipes in pilot.
- >80% usage of the workbench in eligible SRE playbooks in pilot orgs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Workbench prototype deployed behind SSO to pilot team (SRE-oncall) with at least 8 curated recipes.
- Rehearsal mode returns a deterministic diff and does not change prod state.
- Execution logs include user, recipe-version, inputs, outputs, and signed timestamp stored in audit index.
- Ephemeral credentials auto-revoke within configured TTL and are logged.
- Telemetry emits a per-execution metric that appears in Grafana dashboard (workbench.executions.{ok|warn|fail}).

2025-02-19: Implemented server-side rehearsal harness (feature-branch). Rehearsal returns mock state diffs and execution cost estimate.
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal-admin/pull/246
2025-02-24: Security review (initial): recommend RBAC gating + KMS-wrapped ephemeral creds. Security to review final IAM flow. Action: add secure-credential-retriever shim.
2025-02-28: Pilot deploy to staging cluster with 5 recipes. Observability hooks emitting metrics and traces. UX polish pass scheduled next week.
